top_ai_signals.why_it_matters: Named fact-checks and dated public provenance are stronger than a naked model score because they show where the claim came from and whether journalists have already verified or debunked it.
top_ai_signals.caveat: OSINT is strongest for public figures, viral claims, and news events. Generic private images may have no searchable provenance.

top_ai_signals.summary: The file's embedded provenance marks it as AI-generated.
top_ai_signals.what_found: The provenance metadata flags this as trained-algorithmic (AI-generated) media.
top_ai_signals.why_it_matters: Provenance markers like C2PA are an industry-standard, hard-to-fake trace written by the generator itself. Finding one is among the strongest provenance signals available.
top_ai_signals.caveat: Provenance can be stripped or, rarely, forged. Absence of a marker is not proof of authenticity.

top_inconclusive_signals.name: Lighting Physics & Contrast Geometry
top_inconclusive_signals.summary: The lighting is balanced and well-behaved (255/255 range, 38.8/255 mean, 0.058% clipping) - matching both a well-exposed real photo and a capable AI generator.
top_inconclusive_signals.what_found: The image has a 255/255 dynamic range, 38.8/255 mean brightness, and only 0.058% clipped highlights with 0.506% crushed shadows. This balanced exposure is realistic-looking but not diagnostic - it fits equally well for a careful real photograph and a modern AI generator.
top_inconclusive_signals.why_it_matters: Lighting is most useful when it's either suspiciously perfect (AI) or clearly clipping (real). A balanced middle-ground doesn't give us enough to work with, so this signal defers to others.
top_inconclusive_signals.caveat: HDR post-processing, tone mapping, strong flash, and professional retouching can all alter exposure profiles - introducing 'AI-like' qualities into real photos or vice versa.

top_inconclusive_signals.name: Thermal Noise & Sensor Consistency
top_inconclusive_signals.summary: The noise profile is ambiguous - variance 1557.9, 13.0% smooth blocks - midrange values that could belong to either a compressed real photo or a noise-augmented AI image.
top_inconclusive_signals.what_found: The image has variance 1557.9 and 13.0% flat blocks - neither extreme enough to trigger a clear verdict. This ambiguity typically means the image has been compressed, resized, or otherwise processed in a way that erased the original noise fingerprint.
top_inconclusive_signals.why_it_matters: When noise falls in the middle range, it can belong to either side - meaning this signal cannot meaningfully contribute to the verdict. The other detectors carry more weight here.
top_inconclusive_signals.caveat: Heavy compression, denoising, upscaling, or added grain filters can all change the noise profile independently of whether the image was generated or photographed.

top_inconclusive_signals.name: Error Level Analysis (ELA)
top_inconclusive_signals.summary: The ELA map shows moderate, fairly uniform compression residuals (mean: 1.43, quadrant spread: 0.69). No editing seams or compositing artifacts were detected.
top_inconclusive_signals.what_found: Re-saving at quality 90 produced a mean residual of 1.43 with a quadrant spread of only 0.69. The compression stress is consistent across all four quadrants, and only 0.01% of pixels show elevated residuals. This uniform profile suggests the image has a consistent compression history - no obvious signs of region-level editing or compositing.
top_inconclusive_signals.why_it_matters: A uniform ELA profile removes one red flag - there are no obvious editing seams. However, ELA does not tell us whether the image is AI-generated, only that it has not been obviously composited. The other detectors handle the AI vs. real question.
top_inconclusive_signals.caveat: ELA detects editing and compression inconsistency, not AI generation. Social media uploads, repeated saves, and WhatsApp forwarding all degrade this test. It's treated as a weak supporting check.
